long_biography.plain_text:
Brisbane investor Peter Victor Francis Harburg accumulated a group of landmark city workplaces, concentrating on income-producing towers. His private company bought the State Law Building for A$91 million and also held 348 Edward Street, 260 Queen Street and 95 North Quay. Several assets were later sold to institutional purchasers; the last major pair was offered as market demand strengthened. The origins of the capital behind these acquisitions and his present holdings remain undisclosed.

Sport provided a separate arena for Harburg's competitive instincts. After participating in motor racing, he turned to ocean competition and created an enduring team. A friendship with Formula One champion Sir Jack Brabham inspired the Black Jack name carried by successive boats. Harburg entered the Sydney Hobart repeatedly before his crew secured the 2021 first-to-finish prize. His team then achieved three European offshore line-honours results and captured the 2022-23 Mediterranean Maxi Offshore Challenge. The 100-foot racing boat was subsequently sold, leaving the campaign as an established sporting achievement rather than evidence of a current asset.
